name: Axiom Apex VTOL
description: The private VTOL of choice for corporate executives who need to move between cities or between their penthouse and the office without touching the ground. Six seats, each with more computing power than a Tier 1 neighborhood. The Apex can cross the Great Lakes in forty minutes and land on any rooftop pad. It represents the ultimate expression of the GLMZ class divide — personal air travel, faster than commercial, answerable to no schedule but your own.
propulsion: Tilt-rotor VTOL, hydrogen turbine, anti-grav assist
autonomy: Human pilot with full AI backup. Autonomous emergency return.
armament: Classified countermeasure suite, chaff, flares, signal disruption.
common_usage: Executive inter-city transport, emergency extraction, corporate retreat access.
story_hooks: An Apex pilot is ordered to fly a route that takes them through restricted military airspace — and nothing intercepts them
Two Apex VTOLs from rival corponations nearly collide over the lakefront, triggering a corporate incident that escalates far beyond a traffic violation
physical_description: The Axiom Apex is a sleek six-seat VTOL with a narrow fuselage of brushed titanium and reinforced composite panels, its edges weathered by salt spray and industrial fallout from the Lakes. Twin vertical thrusters dominate the rear, their housings scarred from countless rooftop landings, while the cockpit features wraparound laminated glass tinted to reduce thermal signature. Interior surfaces gleam with carbon fiber and supple leather worn smooth by executive use, though the exterior hull bears the faint oxidation marks of a machine that moves between two worlds.
